Q: Can you use the this keyword outside of the non static function member? A:

this can't be used outside member function. It is in fact an implicit (hidden) argument of member function.
Since C++23 there is new syntax to pass this explicitly to member function:

Non-static member functions - explicit object parameter

Explicit object member functions

For a non-static non-virtual member function not declared with cv-qualifier or ref-qualifier, its first parameter, if not being a function parameter pack, can be an explicit object parameter (denoted with the prefixed keyword this):

struct X
{
    void foo(this X const& self, int i); // same as void foo(int i) const &;
//  void foo(int i) const &; // Error: already declared

    void bar(this X self, int i); // pass object by value: makes a copy of “\*this”
};

In old syntax first parameter is hidden under this keyword.

If you see this new syntax for member functions, it becomes obvious why using this outside member function doesn't make sense.

If you try use std::bind with member functions this hidden this argument also becomes more obvious.
